Accenture Song Life—A Partner for Growth 

The Agency of Record model we all grew up with was built for stability—long planning cycles, rigid campaigns, and success measured in outputs. Today demands something more. With evolving pipelines, diverse patient populations, and accelerated launches, the challenge is not just communication—it’s staying continually relevant. 

At Accenture Song Life, we reinvented the AOR to be a true growth engine for biopharma—anchored in one objective: helping you fuel growth by building continual relevance. 

We do this by being Smarter, Faster, Better 

Smarter—intelligence-led, powered by AI, data, and life sciences expertise, so your brand is always one step ahead. 

Faster—an agile, adaptive model that scales global blockbusters and targets rare disease communities with equal precision, moving at the speed of science and patient need. 

Better—world-class creativity combined with Accenture’s technology and consulting rigor, shifting from campaigns to outcomes—like launch uptake, adherence, and market share. 

The reinvented AOR is not a supplier—it’s a growth partner. Accenture Song Life brings creativity, technology, and strategy together to serve as your growth engine—continually relevant, always accountable, and built to deliver impact for patients, providers, and your business.” 

You Are:

Accenture Song is looking for a rare kind of creative engineer — someone who thinks like a strategist, builds like a maker, and operates like an agency of one. This is not a role about managing AI adoption or evangelizing what's possible. It's about doing it: conceiving ideas, assembling the tools, and shipping solutions that didn't exist yesterday.

You'll help reinvent how Accenture Song works and what it sells — turning emerging AI capabilities into real, repeatable offerings that create genuine value for clients. You move fast, work across disciplines, and are equally comfortable in a whiteboard session with a creative director and a working prototype session with a technologist.

The Work:

Invent & Build

  • Act as a creative engineer and maker — not just a recommender. If you can imagine it, you should be able to rough it out.

  • Prototype rapidly: turn a brief, a conversation, or a napkin idea into something tangible that a team can react to and a client can see

  • Design AI-native solutions from scratch — not retrofitted workflows, but experiences and systems built around what AI actually makes possible

  • Bring creative instincts to technical problems and technical instincts to creative ones

Shape & Scale Offerings

  • Work with Song leadership to identify which prototypes have the legs to become formal, repeatable offerings

  • Define what an offering actually is: the problem it solves, the value it delivers, how it's built, and how it gets sold

  • Develop the reusable assets, playbooks, and reference models that let teams deliver it again and again

  • Ensure everything you build is designed for scale — not one-off heroics

Connect the Dots

  • Serve as the connective tissue between strategy, creative, data, technology, and operations — fluent in all of them, siloed in none

  • Help teams choose the right tools for the right job, without attachment to any one platform or approach

  • Make the complex feel simple: translate AI capabilities into plain language that inspires action at the leadership level

  • Facilitate working sessions, sprints, and incubators that move quickly from "what if" to "here's how"

Challenge & Evolve

  • Question established processes — especially the ones people have stopped questioning

  • Advocate for AI-first approaches rather than AI bolted onto the way things have always been done

  • Help the organization distinguish between process optimization and genuine reinvention

  • Identify the organizational friction that slows innovation and work with leadership to clear it

AI Fluency:

You should be comfortable working with AI tools across the creative and technical spectrum — not as an IT specialist, but as a creative practitioner who knows which tool to reach for and why. Familiarity across some of the following is expected:

Generative & Creative AI

  • Claude, ChatGPT/GPT-4o, Gemini — language, reasoning, and content generation

  • Adobe Firefly, Midjourney, Runway — visual ideation, image and video generation within creative workflows

  • Suno, ElevenLabs, or similar — audio and voice generation for experience prototyping

Agentic & Workflow Automation

  • Building agentic workflows — designing multi-step AI systems that can reason, act, and loop with minimal human intervention

  • Orchestration tools — experience with frameworks that connect models, data, and actions into coherent pipelines

  • Low-code and no-code automation — turning complex processes into streamlined, repeatable flows without writing everything from scratch

Prototyping & Rapid Development

  • Vibe coding and AI-assisted development — using tools like Cursor, Copilot, or Claude to build functional prototypes faster than traditional dev cycles allow

  • API integration and prompt engineering — knowing how to connect AI services and get reliable, repeatable outputs

  • Cloud and deployment basics — enough to get a prototype live and in front of stakeholders quickly

Basic Qualifications:

  • 5+ years of experience across AI solution development, digital transformation, creative technology, product innovation, or a related field

Preferred Qualifications:

  • Agency, consulting, innovation lab, or product company experience

  • Work that spans marketing, commerce, experience design, content, creative technology, or enterprise operations

  • Experience building reusable IP: accelerators, toolkits, reference architectures, or commercial offerings

  • Own intake and execution for tickets escalated from the Support queue into the SaaS lane, and write the runbook as you go

Renewals & Vendor Operations

Audit & Compliance Operations

Google Workspace

Slack

  • Auditing and rotating Slack apps credentials in partnership with developers

You may be a good fit if you

  • Have hands-on experience administering a portfolio of SaaS applications at the admin level, ideally in a fast-paced or high-growth environment
  • Have owned license and seat management: assignment, reclamation, and utilization reporting
  • Have supported renewals or true-ups and worked directly with vendor account or CSM contacts
  • Have pulled audit evidence or executed access reviews (SOC2 or a similar framework)
  • Are an excellent communicator who genuinely enjoys helping people solve problems
  • Write things down: runbooks, how-to guides, and knowledge base articles
  • Are organized enough to run calendar-driven work (renewals, audits, access reviews) alongside a ticket queue without things falling through the cracks

  • Have Google Workspace administration experience, especially with Google Groups
  • Have worked a full SOC2 or similar audit cycle on the evidence side
  • Have experience with a SaaS management or license management platform
  • Have experience using AI tools to improve personal or team productivity

Location

This is a remote role. Travel to our San Francisco office is required, along with occasional travel to other Anthropic offices.

What Makes This Role Unique

You'll be among the first people in a newly defined lane, which means the renewal calendar, the utilization reporting, and the runbook are yours to build. The lane spans Anthropic's SaaS catalog and sits at the junction of IT Operations and IT Engineering, so you'll see how the whole company works. And growth out of the lane is broad: people here have moved toward product, project and program management, and SecOps, and experience in this lane is a strong path toward IT Engineering.

Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be received on a rolling basis.

The annual compensation range for this role is listed below.

For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

Annual Salary:
$230,000—$265,000 USD

Logistics

Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit directly for confirmed position openings.

How we're different

We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

Come work with us!

Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. As a vital part of the global Davies Group, we help businesses navigate risk, optimize operations, and spearhead transformation in the insurance and regulated sectors.

Davies North America is seeking an experienced Triage Telephonic Case Manager (RN) to join our Workers' Compensation managed care team. This role is responsible for providing clinical triage and telephonic case management services at the initial report of injury, ensuring injured employees receive appropriate, timely medical care while promoting recovery and return-to-work outcomes.
The ideal candidate is a Registered Nurse with strong clinical assessment skills, workers' compensation knowledge, and the ability to make independent decisions in a dynamic, fast-paced environment. This position plays a critical role in the early intervention process, helping coordinate care, identify barriers to recovery, and advocate for injured workers while balancing client and regulatory requirements.

Shift Availability: We currently have three openings available for this position, including two daytime shifts (9:00 AM - 6:00 PM) and one evening shift (2:00 PM - 11:00 PM). Candidates must be able to work one of these schedules based on business needs and availability.

Key Responsibilities

  • Provide telephonic triage case management services at the onset of workers' compensation claims.
  • Conduct comprehensive clinical assessments of injured employees at the time of injury and determine appropriate levels of care.
  • Complete initial evaluations and required three-point contacts in accordance with state requirements and established protocols.
  • Assess medical appropriateness of treatment and support timely access to care.
  • Develop and implement initial case management care plans based on assessment findings.
  • Coordinate communication among injured workers, employers, providers, claims professionals, and other stakeholders.
  • Identify potential barriers to recovery and document findings for future case planning.
  • Evaluate return-to-work capabilities and facilitate modified duty discussions when appropriate.
  • Monitor treatment plans for compliance with state guidelines, evidence-based protocols, and client-specific requirements.
  • Identify potential causation concerns and communicate findings to appropriate parties.
  • Accurately document all assessments, contacts, medical information, and case activities within the claims management system.
  • Serve as a patient advocate while maintaining compliance with all legal, ethical, and regulatory requirements.
  • Support utilization management efforts through coordination of appropriate medical services and resources.
  • Participate in quality assurance initiatives and departmental projects as assigned.

  • Serve as a resource and mentor to team members as needed.

Skills, knowledge & expertise

    • Critical Care/ICU
    • Occupational Health
    • Industrial Nursing
  • Strong clinical assessment and critical thinking skills.
  • Excellent verbal and written communication skills.
  • Ability to work independently and make sound clinical decisions.
  • Proficiency with Microsoft Office Suite and healthcare or claims-related systems.

Reports To

Director, Global Reliability

Job Type

Full-Time, Exempt

Department

Engineering, Reliability & Automation (ERA)

Organization

Global Supply Chain and Procurement (GPSN)

POSITION SUMMARY

The Sr. Manager, Reliability is a senior technical contributor and program manager within the ERA Global Reliability team, responsible for executing reliability improvement programs across a portfolio of Newell Brands manufacturing sites and distribution centers within the global network of 40+ manufacturing facilities, 60 DCs, and markets in 140 countries. Reporting to the Director, Global Reliability, this role is a field-level executor of the Newell Brands Strategic Equipment Management Policy (SEMP) — the company's governing framework for how assets are planned, acquired, operated, maintained, and retired across the global supply chain network. The Sr. Manager translates SEMP requirements into site-level programs, assessments, and improvement plans, ensuring policy intent is operationalized consistently across assigned sites. This role owns hands-on reliability engineering deliverables: asset criticality assessments, fleet management analysis, condition monitoring program builds, PM optimization, failure mode investigations, and reliability KPI reporting. The Sr. Manager acts as a working technical lead, supporting the fleet management strategy by executing site-level programs that feed network-wide asset intelligence — guiding site-level reliability engineers and maintenance teams through structured improvement initiatives while managing multiple concurrent workstreams and site engagements. This role is a key execution engine for the Global Reliability Program within the ERA Strategic Master Plan.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Reliability Program Execution

  • Execute site-level reliability assessments using the ERA reliability framework: asset registry validation, criticality ranking (FMECA-based), PM plan audit, and condition monitoring gap analysis across manufacturing sites and DC facilities.
  • Develop and implement PM optimization plans using RCM principles, condition-based triggers, and failure mode data; establish PM intervals grounded in equipment OEM data and operational history.
  • Lead condition monitoring program deployment at assigned sites, including vibration analysis routes, oil sampling schedules, thermographic inspection programs, and ultrasound surveys.
  • Execute the Tribo Program at assigned sites: conduct Tribo Scorecard assessments, develop site-level lubrication improvement plans, support development of on-site tribology SMEs, and track progress against network Tribo standards defined by the Director, Global Reliability.
  • Conduct and lead root cause failure analysis (RCFA) investigations for chronic failures and high-impact asset events; own corrective action tracking through closure.
  • Build and maintain failure mode libraries and asset-specific maintenance task lists within MicroMain CMMS.

Fleet Management Execution

  • Execute fleet management assessments within assigned site portfolios: document asset populations by class (motors, drives, compressors, conveyors, automation equipment, etc.), validate fleet criticality ratings, and identify fleet-level PM standardization gaps.
  • Contribute fleet performance data to network-level benchmarking; identify poor-performing assets within a fleet class and recommend lifecycle interventions (condition-based replacement, refurbishment, or standardization).
  • Support the Director in developing capital replacement schedules for critical fleet segments; provide site-level asset condition inputs to long-range capital planning.
  • Implement fleet-based spare parts strategies at assigned sites, including kitting standards and critical spare identification aligned to fleet criticality tiers.

CMMS & Data Management

  • Drive asset data quality within MicroMain: asset hierarchy integrity, PM plan completeness, labor hour capture, and work order classification accuracy.
  • Generate reliability KPI reports including PMR, MTBF, MTTR, planned vs. unplanned maintenance ratio, and backlog analysis at site and regional levels.
  • Support development of reliability analytics dashboards in coordination with the ERA AI & Digital Enablement team.
  • Identify data gaps in CMMS cost fields and labor actuals; develop site-specific data governance improvement plans.

Site Engagement & Coaching

  • Partner with site Engineering Managers and Maintenance Supervisors to build local reliability ownership and PM discipline at the front line.
  • Execute PEAK EFO pillar assessments at assigned sites, evaluating AM and PM pillar maturity against global standards; document gaps, develop site-level improvement plans, and track progression through defined maturity stages in alignment with the Director's network-wide EFO program.
  • Facilitate reliability-focused kaizen events, PM standardization workshops, and condition monitoring training at assigned sites.
  • Support development of site Reliability Engineers through on-site coaching, structured work plans, and technical mentorship.
  • Travel to assigned manufacturing sites (domestic and international) on a regular cadence to assess program execution and drive improvement.

Program Management & Reporting

  • Manage concurrent reliability improvement projects across a portfolio of 4-8 manufacturing sites; maintain project plans, milestone tracking, and risk logs.
  • Report site-level PMR, OEE, and condition monitoring adoption metrics to the Director, Global Reliability on a regular cadence.
  • Participate in PEAK operating reviews, contributing reliability KPIs and site action plans to the monthly/quarterly cadence.
  • Support development of reliability investment business cases, cost avoidance analyses, and capital justification documentation.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Coordinate with ERA Automation and OT teams to integrate condition monitoring sensors and edge devices into the site OT network architecture.
  • Partner with Operations to align reliability program priorities with production scheduling, planned outage windows, and capital projects.

QUALIFICATIONS

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Electrical Engineering, Industrial Engineering, or a related technical discipline.
  • 7+ years of experience in reliability engineering, maintenance engineering, or asset management in a manufacturing environment.
  • Hands-on experience with condition monitoring technologies: vibration analysis, oil analysis, thermography, or equivalent.
  • Experience with CMMS platforms for asset management, PM planning, and work order execution.
  • Working knowledge of RCM, FMECA, PM optimization, and root cause failure analysis methodologies.
  • Demonstrated ability to manage multiple workstreams and site engagements simultaneously.

Preferred

  • CMRP, CRL, or Category I/II vibration analyst certification (ISO 18436 or equivalent).
  • Experience with MicroMain or similar CMMS platforms.
  • Familiarity with PEAK, Lean, or Six Sigma methodologies.
  • International manufacturing site experience; LATAM or EMEA exposure preferred.
  • Experience integrating condition monitoring data with industrial analytics or AI platforms.

COMPETENCIES

  • Strong hands-on technical capability in reliability engineering disciplines
  • Structured problem solver with a data-driven approach to failure analysis
  • Effective communicator with site-level teams and program leadership
  • Self-directed with the ability to manage multiple priorities across a distributed portfolio
  • Collaborative team member with a continuous improvement mindset

jobs.description:
AECOM is seeking a highly experienced Senior Remediation Subject Matter Expert (SME) to provide technical leadership and strategic guidance for complex environmental remediation projects supporting clients in the oil & gas, refining, petrochemical, energy, and industrial sectors. This is a part-time position designed for a recognized industry expert who will serve as a senior technical resource across multiple projects, supporting project delivery, mentoring technical staff, and helping clients develop innovative, cost-effective remediation solutions.

The successful candidate will possess extensive experience with contaminated site investigation and remediation, regulatory compliance, remedial design, and closure strategies. This individual will collaborate with multidisciplinary teams while serving as a trusted advisor to clients and project managers.

The responsibilities of this position include, but are not limited to:

  • Serve as the senior technical lead and subject matter expert for environmental remediation projects involving soil, groundwater, sediment, and vapor impacts.
  • Provide technical oversight and quality reviews for remedial investigations, feasibility studies, corrective action plans, remedial designs, risk assessments, remedial action implementation, and site closure documentation.
  • Develop and review conceptual site models (CSMs), evaluate contaminant fate and transport, and recommend practical, technically sound remediation strategies.
  • Provide technical expertise in the evaluation, selection, and optimization of remediation technologies, including:
  • In-situ Chemical Oxidation (ISCO)Soil Vapor Extraction (SVE)Air SpargingMulti-Phase Extraction (MPE)BioremediationPump and Treat SystemsMonitored Natural Attenuation (MNA)Engineered containment systems
  • Provide strategic guidance for projects regulated under RCRA Corrective Action, CERCLA/Superfund, Brownfields, UST/LUST, and state voluntary cleanup programs.
  • Serve as a senior technical advisor during client meetings, regulatory discussions, and project planning activities.
  • Mentor and provide technical leadership to project managers, engineers, geologists, hydrogeologists, and environmental scientists.
  • Support business development efforts by contributing to technical proposals, scope development, project planning, and client presentations.
  • Collaborate with multidisciplinary engineering and environmental teams to deliver innovative, practical, and cost-effective solutions.
  • Perform senior-level technical reviews to ensure quality, consistency, regulatory compliance, and adherence to AECOM quality standards.
  • Apply strong analytical, problem-solving, communication, and technical writing skills while managing multiple priorities and supporting diverse project teams.
  • Demonstrated experience managing and providing technical oversight for complex remediation projects supporting oil & gas, refinery, petrochemical, industrial, manufacturing, or energy clients.
  • Extensive knowledge of federal and state environmental regulations, including RCRA, CERCLA, UST/LUST programs, and Risk-Based Corrective Action (RBCA).
  • Demonstrated expertise in contaminated site investigation, remedial design, remedy optimization, and regulatory closure.
  • Excellent technical writing, report review, presentation, and client communication skills.
  • Proven ability to mentor technical staff and provide leadership across multidisciplinary project teams.

Minimum Requirements

  • Bachelor's degree in Environmental Engineering, Civil Engineering, Geological Engineering, Geology, Hydrogeology, Environmental Science, or a related field.
  • 12+ years of experience or demonstrated equivalency of experience and/or education.

Preferred Qualifications

  • 20+ years of progressively responsible environmental consulting experience with significant remediation expertise.
  • Professional Engineer (PE) and/or Professional Geologist (PG) registration.
  • Master's degree in Engineering, Hydrogeology, Environmental Science, Geology, or a related discipline.
  • Experience supporting refinery, terminal, pipeline, and upstream or downstream oil & gas remediation projects.
  • Experience with groundwater modeling, contaminant transport modeling, and remedial system optimization.
  • Recognized technical expert with an established reputation within the environmental consulting industry.
  • Strong client relationship management and business development experience, including proposal preparation and strategic client support.

We are hiring a Digital Marketing Manager to act as the digital business owner for a defined portfolio of Force Factor sub-brands, with accountability for driving their growth and overall performance across our eCommerce and retail ecosystem. This role sits inside our Digital Marketing team and reports to the SVP of Digital Marketing.

You will combine performance marketing, retail media, analytics, forecasting, consumer and competitive insights, and rigorous experimentation to understand what is driving the business and determine what we should do next. You will manage significant media investment across Amazon, Walmart, Meta, STV, and other retail and digital channels, but your responsibility extends far beyond media efficiency: you will identify opportunities to accelerate demand, improve paid and organic visibility, acquire new consumers, grow sales, and maximize the profitable long-term growth of your portfolio. You will work closely with Creative, Sales, and eCommerce to make sure every dollar we invest has a clear job to do—and that we are constantly finding better ways to turn that investment into profitable growth.

This is a hands-on seat with real ownership over your slice of the portfolio. You are in the platforms every day for your sub-brands, running the tests, reading the numbers, and moving fast on what they tell you. You will be expected to spot changes in performance early, dig until you understand what is driving them, and turn those findings into clear actions. If you want a role where someone else calls the shots and you execute a plan handed to you, this is not the seat. If you want to own the business performance of a defined portfolio, develop the strategy to grow it, and be accountable for the results, this is exactly the seat.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own the growth strategy and digital business performance for assigned product portfolios, with accountability for POS growth, customer acquisition, media productivity, paid and organic visibility, and profitable long-term growth across eCommerce and key retail channels.
  • Own media strategy, investment, and performance across Amazon Ads, Walmart Connect, Meta, STV, and other priority retail and digital channels, ensuring channel decisions ladder up to broader portfolio and business goals.
  • Develop, execute, and analyze upper-funnel demand generation across STV, paid social (Meta, Instagram, YouTube), display, and emerging channels to expand reach, build brand consideration, acquire new consumers, and understand the downstream impact on retail demand and portfolio growth.
  • Continuously diagnose portfolio performance across sales, traffic, conversion, media, distribution, pricing, promotion, paid and organic search visibility, and competitive activity; identify the true drivers behind changes in performance and turn those findings into clear, actionable growth strategies and new business opportunities.
  • Evaluate media through a total-business and incrementality lens, distinguishing paid from organic contribution, assessing new-to-brand acquisition, and determining when reported channel performance does or does not reflect the true value of the investment.
  • Design and evaluate rigorous tests across media, bidding, audiences, creative, promotional support, and channel mix; separate signal from noise, document learnings, and rapidly scale what works across the portfolio.
  • Use performance data, consumer insights, and structured testing to identify creative opportunities, develop clear briefs and hypotheses, and partner with Creative to continuously improve messaging and asset performance across channels.
  • Translate complex datasets and analyses into concise, decision-ready recommendations for Creative, Sales, eCommerce, and senior leadership, clearly articulating what happened, why it matters, and what we should do next.
  • Own retail media partner relationships, ensuring partners remain aligned to Force Factor’s performance goals and strategic priorities while maintaining internal ownership of strategy and investment decisions.
  • Own portfolio forecasts for POS consumption and media spend; identify variances to plan early, diagnose the drivers, and recommend actions to close performance gaps or accelerate upside.
  • Stay ahead of changes in advertising platforms, retail media capabilities, measurement, attribution, privacy, and consumer behavior, and proactively adapt strategy as things evolve.

Ideal Qualifications

  • Bachelor's degree in a relevant field such as Marketing, Data Analytics, Mathematics, Statistics, Economics, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
  • 4 to 6 years of hands-on performance marketing and retail media experience, including meaningful ownership of multimillion-dollar budgets and business outcomes, not simply campaign execution under someone else's strategy.
  • Experience in CPG, wellness, supplements, or another high-velocity consumer category is strongly preferred.
  • Deep, current fluency across Amazon Ads, Walmart Connect, Meta Ads Manager, STV/CTV, including advanced bidding strategies, audience structures, and performance optimization. Experience with Amazon DSP, AMC, and additional retail media networks is a strong plus.
  • Strong commercial instincts. Evaluates decisions against the health of the overall business, not just CAC, or ROAS, and understands when an apparently “inefficient” investment may still be the right investment to drive incremental and long-term growth
  • Exceptional analytical skills and Excel proficiency. Analytically self-sufficient: comfortable pulling, manipulating, reconciling, and analyzing large or messy datasets, identifying anomalies, pressure-testing conclusions, and building analyses from scratch.
  • Strong understanding of incrementality, attribution, paid versus organic contribution, new-to-brand acquisition, and the limitations of platform-reported performance metrics.
  • Naturally investigative and intellectually curious. When performance changes, you do not simply report what happened, you keep digging until you understand why it happened and what should change as a result.
  • Direct, concise, and confident communicator. You can translate complex analyses into a clear recommendation, explain the business implications to non-marketers and senior leaders, and defend your reasoning without hiding behind jargon.
  • High degree of ownership and autonomy. You identify problems and opportunities without waiting to be assigned them, develop a point of view, and bring solutions and recommendations rather than open-ended questions.
  • A bias for speed and comfort with ambiguity. You test, learn, make decisions with imperfect information, and move again without waiting for a committee, while maintaining a high bar for accuracy and quality.
  • Genuine curiosity about the category and competitive landscape. You know who the important competitors are, pay attention to what they are doing, and form a point of view on where they are winning, where they are vulnerable, and what Force Factor should do differently.
  • Passion for analytics, performance marketing, and continuous learning, with a desire to stay current on emerging advertising capabilities, measurement approaches, retail media trends, and best practices.
  • Well-organized, methodical thinker who can handle competing priorities and make decisions under pressure while delivering accurate, on-time, high-quality work.
  • Detail-oriented, driven, and organized high performer with an insatiable desire to win.

jobs.title: Service Delivery Senior Manager – Software Publisher Services - anywhere in APAC
jobs.excerpt: Service Delivery Manager – Software Publisher Services – anywhere in APAC "Are you looking for an opportunity to drive commercial growth, own strategic client relationships, and shape the future of software compliance advisory at a global level?
jobs.description:
Service Delivery Manager – Software Publisher Services – anywhere in APAC

"Are you looking for an opportunity to drive commercial growth, own strategic client relationships, and shape the future of software compliance advisory at a global level?"

About the Company

Connor Consulting Partners, LLC is a specialist advisory firm delivering software license compliance and advisory services to a global client base.

We are in an exciting period of growth and organisational maturity. Our line of business is structured so that every person operates at their highest value: Directors focus on client outcomes and commercial growth, a dedicated delivery management function provides the operational infrastructure, and Account Managers and Technical Leads run day-to-day execution with genuine autonomy. The result is a firm where the delivery engine is as strong as the commercial engine.

The Opportunity

We are looking for a Delivery Manager / Senior Manager to own and build the delivery infrastructure for our Software Publisher Services practice. This is a pivotal role: you sit at the centre of the organisation, ensuring that every engagement is delivered consistently, every process is documented and followed, and every team member is developed and deployed effectively.

This is not a client-facing commercial role, and it is not a project management role. You will not own client relationships or carry revenue targets. Instead, you will build and maintain the business systems that everyone else relies on: tracking, quality frameworks, resource management, team development, and governance. Your success is measured by the strength of the infrastructure you create and the capability of the teams you grow.

The right person for this role is a systems thinker who finds satisfaction in building infrastructure that scales, who understands that authority comes from demonstrated value rather than positional power, and who can operate effectively across a matrix structure spanning multiple regions and clients.

Key Accountabilities

Governance and Delivery Infrastructure

  • Build, maintain, and continuously improve the tracking, reporting, and process infrastructure that underpins delivery across all clients and regions. This includes project tracking systems, dashboards, documented processes, and engagement lifecycle frameworks.
  • Own the delivery system end-to-end. Your processes and frameworks become business standards that the entire organisation operates within, not optional guidance, but the way we work.
  • Provide the leadership team with the operational data they need to make informed decisions without being operationally involved: delivery status, budget positions, risk indicators, and capacity outlook.

Culture and Team Identity

  • Build and sustain a strong, unified team culture across all regions. Our delivery teams operate as one global team, there is no distinction between onshore and offshore, front office and back office. You are the person who makes that identity real, not just aspirational.
  • Create an environment where people want to do their best work. Culture is not a side project, it is the foundation that every process, framework, and governance cadence is built on. If the culture is wrong, nothing else works at scale.
  • Foster professional pride in delivery standards. When the team sees quality and consistency as part of their identity rather than something imposed on them, you have built something that sustains itself.
  • Connect people across geographies. In a distributed team, culture does not happen by accident. You deliberately create the forums, rituals, and shared experiences that make people feel part of something larger than their individual engagement.
  • Champion inclusion and professional development as core cultural values. Every team member, regardless of region, role level, or tenure, should see a clear path forward and feel invested in by the organisation.

Quality Framework

  • Design, maintain, and enforce the quality frameworks, checklists, and processes that ensure consistent delivery standards across every engagement. Directors set the quality expectations for their clients; you build the infrastructure that reliably delivers against those expectations.
  • Identify quality and consistency issues across regions before they reach clients. You are the organisation's early warning system for systemic delivery risks.
  • Drive continuous improvement in quality outcomes through data, process refinement, and structured governance.

Resource and Capacity Management

  • Manage the shared resource pool across regions. Assess capability, track availability, and prepare staffing recommendations for Director decisions.
  • Build and maintain a rolling capacity view so the organisation can plan proactively rather than react to resourcing gaps.
  • Own time-to-fill performance, ensuring that engagements are staffed with the right people quickly and efficiently.

Team Development

  • Primary owner of career development, skills frameworks, and training for the delivery and technical teams. You are responsible for growing the capability of the people who deliver our work.
  • Conduct skills assessments, identify development needs, and build training programmes that close gaps systematically.
  • Manage onboarding effectiveness, ensuring new team members are productive and contributing within a defined timeframe.
  • Initiate and manage performance improvement plans where needed. You own the people development infrastructure.

What We Expect in Return

This role carries significant organisational influence. With that comes a set of commitments we expect:

  • Build your authority through demonstrated value. When the infrastructure you create makes people's jobs easier and delivery more consistent, compliance becomes a professional standard, not something you have to enforce.
  • Be transparent about delivery risks. Your role is to surface reality, not to filter it. The leadership team depends on your data to make good decisions.
  • Prioritise quick wins. Sequence your work so that the organisation sees value early. Each piece of infrastructure you deliver builds the trust needed for the next.
  • Work collaboratively with Directors as a genuine partner. They own the client relationships; you provide the infrastructure that supports them. Engage constructively, share information openly, and treat each other's domains with respect.
  • Protect the team culture you build. As the organisation grows, the culture either scales deliberately or it dilutes. You are accountable for making sure it scales.

How This Role Works Day-to-Day

We have deliberately structured this role to sit at the centre of the organisation, connected to every function but operating in a distinct lane. Here is what that looks like in practice:

Your focus

Delivery infrastructure, quality frameworks, process design, resource management, team development, and operational governance across all clients and regions.

Not your focus

Client commercial relationships, revenue targets, new business development, or day-to-day client communication — we have dedicated Directors and Account Managers for this.

Your governance rhythm

Structured weekly and monthly forums with the leadership team and delivery teams. You provide the data, analysis, and recommendations that inform decisions across the business.

How you get things done

Through infrastructure and influence. You build systems that people rely on because they make delivery better. Your authority comes from the value of what you build, not from hierarchy.

What your teams handle

Day-to-day client delivery, project management, routine budget conversations, and engagement execution — all owned by Account Managers and Technical Leads operating within the frameworks you build.

About You

Experience & Knowledge

  • Significant experience in delivery management, operations management, or programme management within a professional services or advisory environment. You understand what it takes to build delivery infrastructure that scales across multiple clients and regions.
  • Experience in software license compliance, software asset management, or a related technology advisory field is highly desirable. Understanding the audit lifecycle and client engagement model will accelerate your impact.
  • Proven track record of building governance systems, quality frameworks, and operational processes, either from scratch or by significantly improving existing ones. You can point to the infrastructure you built and the outcomes it produced.
  • Experience managing a shared resource pool or bench model. You understand capacity planning, skills assessment, and the dynamics of matching people to engagements.
  • International delivery experience. Our teams operate across APAC, EMEA, and the Americas. You are comfortable working across time zones and cultures and understand the challenge of maintaining consistency at a distance.
  • Experience with delivery tracking tools, dashboards, and reporting systems. You are comfortable with data and use it to drive decisions and surface risks.

Leadership & Competencies

  • Systems thinker. You see the whole picture and design infrastructure that connects the parts. You think in processes, frameworks, and feedback loops, not just individual tasks.
  • Influence without authority. You build credibility through demonstrated value. You can get things done in a matrix structure where people do not report directly to you, and you understand that the best systems are the ones people want to use.
  • Builder mentality. You find genuine satisfaction in creating infrastructure that others rely on. You would rather build a system that works without you than be the person everything depends on.
  • Collaborative partner. You work effectively with senior commercial leaders who have different priorities and pressures. You provide data and recommendations without overstepping into their decision-making authority.
  • Culture builder. You understand that a strong team culture is not a byproduct of good process, it is a prerequisite. You have built or shaped team cultures before, particularly across distributed or multi-regional teams, and you know how to make people feel connected to something larger than their individual work.
  • People developer. You invest in growing your team's capability because you understand that team quality is infrastructure. Skilled, confident people are the foundation everything else is built on.
  • Transparent communicator. You surface reality. You present data honestly, flag risks early, and never filter information to make things look better than they are.

Qualifications

  • Degree-level education or equivalent professional experience.
  • Relevant certifications in project management, delivery management, or quality frameworks are advantageous (e.g., PMP, PRINCE2, ITIL, Six Sigma, or similar).
  • ITAM, SAM, or vendor-specific compliance certifications are a plus but not required.

What We Offer

  • A role at the centre of a specialist advisory firm's operating model. You are not a support function, you are the person who builds the infrastructure that makes the entire delivery engine work.
  • An organisational structure where your role has clear authority. The delivery standards and processes you build are treated as business infrastructure that the entire leadership team reinforces.
  • Directors who actively champion the delivery standards you set. You are not fighting for relevance, the organisation is designed so that every function depends on the systems you maintain.
  • The opportunity to build from a strong foundation. We have a growing client base, capable delivery teams, and senior leadership commitment to operational excellence. Your job is to build the infrastructure that takes us from good to consistently excellent.
  • A collaborative leadership team that values transparency, shared information, and mutual support.
  • Competitive compensation package commensurate with the strategic importance and organisational impact of the role.

Benefits - Why Connor?

We approach every relationship with purpose, attention, and a little fun! You can expect a flexible working environment, paid mental health days, a generous vacation package, and competitive compensation. You’ll be working with a highly driven, collaborative global team that values trust, accountability, and continuous learning. We nurture our people in a culture that promotes diversity and individuality that sparks innovation and creativity.

Connor Consulting Partners, LLC is an equal opportunity employer and values diversity, equality, and inclusion. We do not discriminate based on race, religion, color, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.

If you are a professional who is looking for an opportunity where you can put your honed skills and abilities to work for a mission that you are passionate about, then this is the right career opportunity for you.

Join us and be part of our Global Team. Apply now!

jobs.description:
Controller (Financial Reporting, GAAP/IFRS & Accounting Leadership) – Remote | U.S. Hours

Position Type: Full-Time, Remote
Working Hours: U.S. Business Hours

About the Role

At Pavago, one of our clients is hiring an experienced Controller to lead accounting operations, financial reporting, compliance, internal controls, and finance team performance.

This is a senior, hands-on accounting leadership role with ownership across:

  • Month-end and year-end close
  • GAAP/IFRS financial reporting
  • Internal controls and audit readiness
  • Cash flow and treasury management
  • Budgeting and forecasting support
  • Accounting team leadership
  • ERP and process improvements

You’ll work closely with executive leadership and FP&A to maintain accurate financials, strengthen accounting operations, and turn financial data into actionable business insights.

If you have deep accounting expertise, strong leadership experience, and can balance financial control with strategic decision support, this role is a strong fit.

What You’ll Own

Month-End & Year-End Close

  • Own monthly, quarterly, and year-end close processes
  • Drive a 5-business-day month-end close
  • Review and approve:
    • Journal entries
    • Accruals
    • Balance sheet reconciliations
    • Supporting schedules
  • Ensure general ledger accuracy and completeness
  • Prepare and review consolidated:
    • Profit & Loss Statements
    • Balance Sheets
    • Cash Flow Statements
  • Identify and resolve accounting discrepancies before reporting deadlines

Financial Reporting & Analysis

  • Prepare accurate GAAP/IFRS-compliant financial statements
  • Deliver timely monthly and quarterly reporting packages
  • Perform budget-to-actual and period-over-period variance analysis
  • Translate financial results into clear insights for executive leadership
  • Support:
    • Board reporting
    • Investor reporting
    • Executive dashboards
    • Management reporting
  • Provide financial recommendations that support business decision-making

Internal Controls, Audit & Compliance

  • Design, implement, and maintain effective internal controls
  • Strengthen accounting policies, procedures, and approval workflows
  • Ensure compliance with applicable regulatory, accounting, and tax requirements
  • Manage external audit processes
  • Prepare and coordinate PBC (Prepared by Client) schedules
  • Maintain organized, audit-ready financial documentation
  • Proactively identify financial and compliance risks

Budgeting & Forecasting

  • Partner with FP&A and leadership on annual budgets and forecasts
  • Analyze financial performance against plans
  • Support scenario planning and capital allocation decisions
  • Provide accounting and financial insights for strategic initiatives
  • Help leadership understand financial risks, opportunities, and trade-offs

Treasury & Cash Management

  • Monitor cash flow, liquidity, and working capital
  • Maintain visibility into short- and long-term cash requirements
  • Support cash planning and treasury operations
  • Oversee debt compliance and credit facilities
  • Help maintain financial stability as the organization grows

Accounting Team Leadership

  • Lead, mentor, and manage accountants and finance team members
  • Delegate responsibilities and establish clear priorities
  • Review team outputs for accuracy and completeness
  • Develop team capabilities and strengthen accounting discipline
  • Establish high standards for:
    • Accuracy
    • Timeliness
    • Documentation
    • Accountability

Systems & Process Improvement

  • Identify inefficiencies across accounting and reporting workflows
  • Lead or support ERP implementations and system improvements
  • Automate repetitive accounting and reporting processes
  • Develop and improve financial SOPs
  • Strengthen scalability as transaction volume and organizational complexity increase
  • Improve financial visibility through better systems, reporting, and controls

Required Experience & Skills

Must-Have

  • Bachelor’s degree in Accounting, Finance, or a related field
  • 7+ years of progressive accounting or finance experience
  • 2+ years of accounting leadership or supervisory experience
  • Strong knowledge of GAAP and/or IFRS
  • Proven experience owning month-end and year-end close
  • Strong financial statement preparation and reporting experience
  • Experience designing or maintaining internal controls
  • Experience supporting or managing external audits
  • Hands-on experience with ERP/accounting systems such as:
    • NetSuite
    • SAP
    • Oracle
    • QuickBooks Enterprise
  • Advanced Excel / Google Sheets proficiency
  • Strong analytical and problem-solving abilities
  • Excellent written and verbal English communication
  • Comfortable leading teams remotely during U.S. business hours

Nice to Have

  • CPA, ACCA, MBA, or equivalent professional qualification
  • Previous experience as a Controller, Assistant Controller, or Finance Manager
  • ERP implementation or accounting system migration experience
  • M&A integration experience
  • Multi-entity or consolidated accounting experience
  • Background in:
    • SaaS
    • Professional services
    • Real estate
  • Experience with BI and reporting platforms such as:
    • Power BI
    • Tableau
    • Looker

What Makes You a Strong Fit

  • You take full ownership of financial accuracy and reporting
  • You can lead a finance team while remaining hands-on when needed
  • You understand both the technical and operational sides of accounting
  • You proactively identify financial risks and control weaknesses
  • You can translate complex financial information into clear executive insights
  • You build scalable processes rather than relying on manual workarounds
  • You hold yourself and your team to high standards for accuracy and deadlines
  • You’re comfortable partnering directly with senior leadership

What a Typical Day Looks Like

You might start by reviewing close progress, reconciliations, cash position, and outstanding accounting items.

Throughout the day, you’ll review financial statements and journal entries, analyze variances, collaborate with FP&A and leadership, respond to audit or compliance requirements, and provide guidance to accounting team members.

You’ll also work on longer-term improvements such as ERP optimization, automation, internal controls, and accounting SOPs.

In short: you own the financial control environment—ensuring leadership has accurate numbers, reliable processes, and clear financial visibility.

Key Metrics for Success

  • Month-end close completed within 5 business days
  • Accurate and timely financial statements
  • Zero material audit adjustments
  • 100% on-time compliance and required filings
  • Strong balance sheet reconciliation accuracy
  • Reliable cash flow and liquidity visibility
  • Improved accounting workflow efficiency
  • High-performing and accountable finance team
  • Clear, actionable financial insights for leadership

Tools & Technology

  • NetSuite
  • SAP
  • Oracle
  • QuickBooks Enterprise
  • Microsoft Excel
  • Google Sheets
  • Power BI
  • Tableau
  • Looker

Why This Role Stands Out

  • Full ownership of a high-impact accounting function
  • Direct collaboration with executives and senior leadership
  • Opportunity to influence financial and operational decision-making
  • Leadership responsibility with meaningful team ownership
  • Opportunity to improve ERP systems, controls, and accounting processes
  • Fully remote environment
  • Growth potential into:
    • Senior Controller
    • Corporate Controller
    • VP of Finance
    • Finance Leadership

Interview Process

  1. Initial Screening Call
  2. Recruiter Interview
  3. Client / Leadership Interview
  4. Offer & Onboarding

Apply Now

If you’re an experienced Controller or accounting leader who can own financial reporting, lead close processes, strengthen controls, develop teams, and provide leadership with reliable financial insights, we’d love to hear from you.

Apply today and take ownership of a finance function where accuracy, leadership, and strategic financial visibility directly impact business growth.

jobs.description:
ABOUT UNBOUNDED

We are a team of former classroom teachers, district and school leaders, curriculum writers, and education experts unified by our desire to see every student thrive in school.

Our commitment to every learner unites us. UnboundEd works side-by-side with teachers, coaches, principals, and district leaders to ensure every student has access to grade-level, engaging, affirming, and meaningful — GLEAM™ — instruction. By cultivating the mindsets, knowledge, and skills at the heart of truly transformative teaching and learning, we can break the predictability of historic achievement patterns so all kids thrive.

In 2023, UnboundEd joined forces with Pivot Learning and CORE Learning to expand our offerings and drive long-needed changes in instruction, especially in the highest-need schools.

Requirements

POSITION SUMMARY

Reporting to the Senior Vice President, Digital Products, the Digital Products Manager is a key member of UnboundEd’s Digital Products division, responsible for managing the lifecycle of digital platforms that support educators nationwide. This role focuses on the development, scaling, and continuous improvement of core products, including Onyx (an AI-enabled instructional design platform) and the Online Math Academy (OMA).

The Digital Products Manager will ensure all digital solutions align with UnboundEd’s mission to provide GLEAM™ instruction to historically marginalized students.

UnboundEd is a virtual organization, and this exempt position can be based anywhere in the United States. UnboundEd has core business hours, during which we expect all staff to be available from 9 am to 5 pm local time.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Essential responsibilities for this position include, but are not limited to:

Product Lifecycle & Strategy

  • Manage the product roadmap for UnboundEd's core digital products (including Onyx and OMA), balancing near-term feature updates with long-term infrastructure and scalability goals.
  • Collaborate with technical and non-technical stakeholders to define product requirements and translate them into executable technical specifications.
  • Lead the transition and integration of products into the Canvas LMS environment, ensuring seamless data acquisition and system interoperability.

Cross-Functional Collaboration

  • Partner with content, program design, and research teams to ensure digital tools reflect high-quality instructional materials (HQIM) and evidence-based professional learning.
  • Work closely with Sales and Marketing representatives to support product rollout, user onboarding, and market positioning.
  • Act as a bridge between technical engineering teams and organizational leadership, providing clarity on progress, impact, and roadblocks.

User-Centric Design & Inclusion

  • Champion a user-centric approach by incorporating educator feedback and research into product iterations.
  • Ensure all digital products meet the highest standards of accessibility, security, and usability, specifically tailored for educators serving Multilingual Learners.
  • Utilize analytics and performance data to monitor KPIs and drive data-informed improvements to the user experience.

Agile Delivery

  • Implement and lead agile project management methodologies (e.g., SCRUM) to ensure the timely delivery of high-quality software.
  • Facilitate the creation and prioritization of product backlogs, managing the "leave-behind" practice-embedded learning artifacts for educators.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education:

  • Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Product Development, Education, or a related field required (Master’s degree preferred).

Experience:

  • Minimum of 3+ years of professional experience in product management, EdTech, or related technology project management roles.

Technical Skills & Competencies:

  • Demonstrated experience driving complex projects in an agile/software development environment; CSPO or similar certification is a plus.
  • Familiarity with AI-enabled tools, LMS platforms (specifically Canvas), and data-sharing/CRM protocols (e.g., Salesforce, Qualtrics).
  • Proven ability to analyze varied problems and implement solutions using data, general precedents, and standard EdTech practices.

The strongest candidates will demonstrate:

  • Strong understanding of adult learning design and research-based instructional practices.
  • Strong communication skills, with the ability to bridge complex technical concepts and non-technical stakeholders.
  • Commitment to UnboundEd’s organizational values and mission.
  • A learning orientation and dedication to equity and inclusion.
  • Knowledge of urban school environments.
  • Ability to work independently in a remote setting while building strong cross-geography relationships.
  • A collaborative spirit and eagerness to contribute to a highly engaged team.
  • Entrepreneurial drive and adaptability in a fast-paced, evolving environment.
  • Proficiency with Google Workspace and collaboration tools such as Slack.

Benefits

COMPENSATION AND BENEFITS

UnboundEd offers competitive salaries commensurate with experience. The annual salary hiring range for this position is $84,700 to $119,650. UnboundEd bases compensation offers on relevant years of experience, internal equity, and company budgets. Because of our strong commitment to equity and growth, UnboundEd does not negotiate compensation offers.

We also offer a generous benefits package that includes take-as-you-need vacation time, group medical, dental, and vision plans, disability and life insurance plans, and an employer-sponsored 401K retirement plan with a 5% employer contribution and no vesting period.

Beyond pay and benefits, UnboundEd offers a collaborative, mission-driven environment where your work directly impacts educators and students nationwide.

jobs.excerpt: Space Inch continues to grow!  Following a string of successful hires, we keep on growing our engineering team.
jobs.description:
Space Inch continues to grow! Following a string of successful hires, we keep on growing our engineering team.

We’re looking for a hands-on Engineering Manager to join one of our longest-running and most successful projects. This is a hybrid role where you’ll spend roughly 75%+ of your time coding as a senior Java engineer, while also leading a small engineering team and acting as the primary day-to-day technical point of contact for the client.

This is a hybrid role: you’ll spend the majority of your time hands-on in the codebase, while also leading a small engineering team, helping organize delivery, mentoring engineers, and acting as the day-to-day technical point of contact for the client. If you enjoy staying close to the technology while also taking ownership of a team and its relationship with the client, we’d love to hear from you.

Our Mission, Vision, and Values

At Space Inch, we prioritize alignment with our clients and team, ensuring a deep understanding of their needs. We are committed to delivering exceptional work while supporting the personal and professional growth of our team members.

Our Stance on AI and Technology Transitions

We don't just "accept" AI; we encourage its usage to enhance productivity and code quality. We’re looking for engineers who are comfortable incorporating AI into their everyday workflow while still applying strong technical judgment knowing how to validate, challenge, and improve AI-generated output.

About Working at Space Inch

  • Our team is around 80 people, primarily based in Croatia, with members across South America, Serbia, and the US; our product team is mostly in the US, with engineering primarily in Croatia and Brazil
  • We are remote-first, though occasional travel may be required, e.g. for our annual company retreats
  • We work on end-to-end projects with a long-term vision
  • We prioritize work-life balance, even with a globally distributed team

Requirements

  • 1–2+ years of hands-on engineering leadership experience, leading a small team while remaining actively involved in the codebase and technical decision-making
  • 7+ years of professional software development experience
  • 5+ years of hands-on experience with Java, Spring, and Spring Boot
  • Strong backend engineering and software architecture fundamentals, with experience building and maintaining production systems and microservices
  • Strong experience with relational databases, particularly PostgreSQL
  • Experience with Docker and cloud environments
  • Familiarity with CI/CD, Kubernetes, and modern cloud infrastructure
  • Comfortable owning the full software development lifecycle, from design through production
  • Experience mentoring engineers, providing technical guidance, and supporting their professional growth
  • Comfortable organizing priorities, tracking delivery, and unblocking a team
  • Experience communicating directly with clients or external stakeholders
  • Comfortable discussing technical decisions, delivery, risks, and priorities with non-engineering stakeholders
  • Familiarity with AI-assisted engineering tools such as Claude, Cursor, or similar, with the ability to validate and improve AI-generated output
  • Strong ownership and accountability
  • Fluent professional English, written and spoken
  • This role is open to candidates currently based in Brazil only.

Key Responsibilities

Engineering — ~75%

  • Build and maintain backend applications and microservices using Java, Spring, and Spring Boot
  • Own technical decisions across architecture and system design
  • Write production-ready code, participate in code reviews, and maintain engineering quality
  • Debug and improve performance, reliability, and scalability
  • Work across databases, cloud infrastructure, CI/CD, and DevOps
  • Use AI-assisted development tools thoughtfully to improve productivity and code quality

Team Leadership & Client Communication — <25%

  • Coordinate planning, prioritization, delivery, and unblocking for a small engineering team
  • Provide technical guidance, mentorship, and feedback
  • Act as the primary day-to-day technical point of contact for the client
  • Communicate progress, risks, priorities, and dependencies proactively
  • Translate client requirements into clear, actionable work and keep the client, team, and Space Inch aligned

What Will Make You Successful

  • You enjoy keeping both the engineering team and client aligned
  • You’re comfortable switching between coding, technical decisions, mentoring, and client communication
  • You take ownership, make decisions independently, and communicate risks early
  • You care about technical quality, team growth, and client experience
  • You’re curious about new technologies and how AI can make engineering teams more effective
  • You lead through technical credibility, context, and communication, rather than hierarchy

This Role Is a Good Fit If

  • You want to remain primarily hands-on while taking on meaningful leadership responsibility
  • You’ve led a small team and enjoy the mix of coding, mentoring, and coordination
  • You’re comfortable being the technical face of the team to the client
  • You thrive in a remote, distributed environment with a high degree of autonomy

This Role Probably Isn’t for You If

  • You’re looking to move completely away from hands-on engineering
  • Your experience is primarily people management rather than technical leadership
  • You prefer someone else to handle client communication and team delivery
  • You’d rather focus exclusively on your own technical tasks than take ownership of the team’s outcomes

Benefits

What's In It for You

  • Real influence on technical decisions and project direction
  • Professional development support
  • Work-life balance, transparency, and long-term relationships that aren’t just for show

Compensation and Benefits

  • Compensations: $4.500,00 – $6.500/monthly for B2B engagement, based on experience and skills.
  • Remote-first setup
  • Health & Wellbeing: Generous PTO + 100% Paid sick leave + Annual health checkup
  • Stay active: Wellness subsidy
  • Continuous Growth: An education budget specifically designed to fuel your learning and help you expand your knowledge base.
  • Extra perks: Referral bonus

Space Inch is not responsible for any job boards scraping this ad without showing the position as remote, but Brazil exclusive. Applicants from other countries will not be considered.

Space Inch is committed to providing an environment of equal employment opportunity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, color, religion, sex (including pregnancy, sexual orientation, or gender identity), national origin, age, disability, genetic information, or any other characteristic protected by applicable law.

This commitment extends to all aspects of employment, including recruitment, hiring, training, promotion, compensation, benefits, and termination. Space Inch believes in treating all employees and applicants with respect and dignity, fostering a workplace where everyone has the opportunity to succeed.

At Mitacs, we take a talent first approach to building Canada’s innovation capacity. We connect researchers with organizations across every region of the country to help solve pressing challenges and accelerate economic growth. By enabling business academic collaboration and supporting the development of highly skilled talent, we contribute to a resilient, future ready Canadian economy.

Guided by our values — Impact, Integrity, Collaboration, Excellence, and Talent — we work with partners nationwide to advance research, commercialization, and innovation.

At Mitacs, you become part of a team committed to empowering Canadian talent, fostering meaningful partnerships, and driving innovation that supports Canada’s long-term competitiveness. If you’re inspired by big ideas and passionate about creating national impact, we encourage you to apply.

About the Policy Team

The Policy team at Mitacs plays a central role in translating complexity into clear, actionable insight. We transform data into informed decisions, develop evidence-based rationales for new initiatives, and articulate the organization’s impact in ways that resonate with government and partners. We ensure that Mitacs programs align with public priorities, clarify the underlying purpose of our work, and provide the policy intelligence and strategic advice necessary to support organizational transformation.

We collaborate closely with Programs, Government Relations, and Evaluations to ensure that Mitacs’s strategies, programs, and proposals are grounded in robust evidence, responsive to public-sector priorities, and communicated effectively to funders and stakeholders.

The Senior Policy Advisor is a strategic thinker, researcher, and storyteller who will help support Mitacs’s evolution and implement its new strategic plan. A key function of this role is conducting original research that identifies emerging trends, risks, and opportunities—providing the organization with strategic advice for policy alignment and organizational transformation.

You will translate complex data into actionable insights, develop compelling narratives for government funders, and support evidence-informed program design. You will lead priority policy files, drive forward-looking analysis, and help shape the strategic direction of the organization.

Key Responsibilities

Strategic Policy Research & Foresight

  • Conduct original policy research, environmental scans, and jurisdictional analyses to inform Mitacs’s evolution and long-term direction.
  • Identify new opportunities in research, innovation, talent development, and economic policy that should shape Mitacs programs and partnerships.
  • Demonstrate how emerging federal/provincial priorities may impact Mitacs, and provide actionable recommendations for organizational alignment.

Organizational Strategy & Transformation

  • Provide evidence-informed policy advice that supports organizational transformation, modernization, and alignment with stakeholder expectations.
  • Identify policy gaps, risks, and opportunities to strengthen Mitacs’s positioning within the broader innovation ecosystem.
  • Develop strategic insights that help executives make decisions about new directions, partnerships, and funding opportunities.

Program Development & Evaluation Integration

  • Articulate the rationale behind new programs and pilots by grounding them in research, evaluation findings, and public priorities.
  • Work with Program teams to interpret evaluation data and recommend whether programs should be scaled, adapted, or sunset.
  • Contribute to theories of change, logic models, and other foundational policy materials.

Government Relations Support & Funding Proposals

  • Produce intelligence briefs, strategic insights, and tailored messaging that help Government Relations engage funders.
  • Co-author funding proposals that draw on policy analysis, program impact, and organizational strategy.
  • Track government mandates, budget cycles, and policy developments to inform both immediate and long-term organizational strategy.

Impact Communication & Storytelling

  • Collaborate with Evaluations to translate program results into compelling stories for governments, partners, and internal stakeholders.
  • Develop content for panels, events, and public communications to clearly articulate Mitacs’s impact.
  • Ensure that data, insights, and narratives are aligned with Mitacs’s strategic objectives and funder expectations.

Qualifications & Experience

  • Graduate degree in public policy, economics, political science, sociology, or a related field preferred.
  • 5–8+ years of experience in federal level policy analysis, public-sector research, strategic planning, or government-related roles. Federal Government experience is a strong asset.
  • Proven experience conducting original policy research that informs strategy or program design.
  • Strong understanding of government decision-making, funding processes, and public-sector priorities.
  • Exceptional writing and communication skills—able to distill complexity into compelling stories.
  • Experience contributing to organizational strategy or transformation initiatives is a strong asset.
  • Comfort working with data, evaluation findings, and qualitative/quantitative research methods.
  • Knowledge of innovation, research, or economic development policy is an advantage.

What You Bring

  • A strategic mindset that connects research insights to organizational decision-making.
  • Curiosity and the ability to uncover the “why” behind issues and programs.
  • Strong analytical capabilities paired with excellent storytelling instincts.
  • A collaborative approach and the ability to influence across teams.
  • Comfort working in an evolving environment where policy, strategy, and program delivery intersect.

Typically, employees are hired, transferred, or promoted within the salary range, specifically between the minimum and midpoint in the hiring range.

Only in rare and exceptional circumstances, where a candidate has the experience, skills, and expertise that far exceed those required for the position, would we consider paying above the hiring range for this role.

Good administration is invisible, and you take quiet pride in that. A registration filed on time, a contract without a single wrong figure, a move-in where the keys are simply there. You hold a deadline because it is a deadline, you treat other people's personal data the way you would want yours treated, and when a case does not fit the process, you take ownership and stay on it until it is resolved.

If that describes you, you are in the right place with us.

As Property Management Associate you are the administrative backbone of property management. You relieve our Property Manager Specialists of standardised, process-driven work along the entire tenancy lifecycle, from move-in preparation through contract administration to move-out, and you execute it reliably, precisely and on time, so they can focus on the judgement-heavy property and customer matters.

The model for the role is the property management assistant as it is established in Swiss real estate: you prepare and execute standard tasks independently, you prepare cases to the point where the Property Manager can take an informed decision, and you recognise the ones that genuinely need their attention. Your work is measured on what shows in the work itself: contracts, registrations and orders that are simply correct, complete and on time, and data quality in the Room Estate system.

Tasks

The work is back-office: you prepare documents, you keep records correct and you handle standardised correspondence such as registrations, service orders and forms. Individual conversations with tenants, landlords and service partners sit with our Customer Excellence and Property Manager Specialists.

  • You administer leases across their entire lifecycle, from the first contract through to the final amendment.
  • You register tenants with the authorities on move-in and deregister them on move-out, always within the statutory deadlines.
  • You prepare move-ins administratively, from key receipts to everything else that has to be in place before someone arrives.
  • You prepare lease amendments at the request of the Property Manager Specialist, who stays accountable for the content.
  • You process defect reports to our service partners and trigger service orders, such as end-of-tenancy cleanings or mailbox label orders.
  • You prepare the official initial-rent forms required by law.
  • You keep partner and rep data current in the Room Estate system and make sure our service partners are correctly assigned to the communities.
  • You verify the identity and solvency of tenants and prospective tenants against the documents on file, and you handle what you see with discretion.
  • You process residence confirmations wherever the standard process applies.
  • You work independently inside the standard processes and escalate only what genuinely needs the Property Manager, prepared to the point where they can decide.

Requirements

  • English, fluent in writing, at a level that carries written administration and internal communication flawlessly.
  • Precision and attention to detail. Contracts, registrations and forms have to be correct the first time, not corrected later.
  • Process discipline, you follow documented processes exactly, you recognise deviations, and you escalate instead of improvising.
  • Ownership and accountability, you take on a matter and drive it to completion, you leave no loop open and you stand behind the quality and timeliness of your work.
  • Self-organisation and reliability, remote. You work independently, structured and deadline-driven without on-site supervision.
  • Digital fluency, you are comfortable in the Room Estate system and standard office tools. Data quality is a core deliverable here, not an afterthought.
  • Discretion, you handle personal data (identity, solvency, residence) confidentially and with care.
